entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 25962 of 2023

Applicant :- Ashish Nishad
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Aarushi Khare,Suneel Kumar Yadav
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Suneel Kumar Yadav for the complainant as well as learned AGA and perused the record.
2. The accused-applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.137 of 2023 under sections 376 IPC and section 3/4 POCSO Act and section 3(2)(v) SC/ST Act, Police Station Kotwali, District Azamgarh.

3. The FIR in question was lodged alleging that on 12.03.2023 the applicant had forced the victim Ashish Nishad vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73842294/
1 into his house and had committed the offence in question.

entities.text: Ashish Nishad vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Exactly same statement was made by the victim in her statements under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., the said statements on record demonstrate that the statements were copy paste of the version given in the FIR.
4. The counsel for the applicant argues that in-similarity in the statements in the FIR and the statements under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. are itself indicative of the biased malice prosecution.

He further argues that the medical report on record does not support the prosecution story and in fact he draws my attention to the medical report on record which indicates the hymen to be old hymen and torn and there are no marks of any physical injury.
The applicant is said to be in custody since 14.03.2023 and has no criminal history.

5. Considering the nature of the allegations levelled in the FIR, the statements under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.being photocopies of the allegations, however, they being at huge variance with the medical report which does not corroborate prima-facie, the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail, more so when he has no criminal history and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail can adversely affect the trial.

6. Let the applicant Ashish Nishad be released on bail in aforesaid first information report number subject to his furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties of Rs.25000/- (Twenty Five Thousand) each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 18.12.2023 VNP/-
